body:
## Problem

Windows CI sometimes fails randomly, where the symptom is: every test starts reporting "nvim crashed". There is no specific test where this occurs, it starts at a random point.

Example:

```
RUN      T610 nvim_set_keymap, nvim_del_keymap can set mappings with special characters, lhs: <S-Left>, rhs: <S-Left>: 93.70 ms OK
RUN      T611 nvim_set_keymap, nvim_del_keymap can set mappings with special characters, lhs: <S-Left>, rhs: <F12><F2><Tab>: 49.48 ms FAIL
D:/a/neovim/neovim/test\functional\testnvim.lua:144: EOF was received from Nvim. Likely the Nvim process crashed.
stack traceback:
	D:/a/neovim/neovim/test/functional/testnvim.lua:144: in function 'nvim_set_keymap'
	.../build/Xtest_xdg_api/test/functional/api/keymap_spec.lua:769: in function <.../build/Xtest_xdg_api/test/functional/api/keymap_spec.lua:768>
RUN      T612 nvim_set_keymap, nvim_del_keymap can set mappings with special characters, lhs: <S-Left>, rhs: <Space><Tab>: 18.49 ms FAIL
D:/a/neovim/neovim/test\functional\testnvim.lua:144: EOF was received from Nvim. Likely the Nvim process crashed.
stack traceback:
	D:/a/neovim/neovim/test/functional/testnvim.lua:144: in function 'nvim_set_keymap'
	.../build/Xtest_xdg_api/test/functional/api/keymap_spec.lua:769: in function <.../build/Xtest_xdg_api/test/functional/api/keymap_spec.lua:768>
```

## Analysis

AI analysis (which sounds very plausible):

> That signature — random onset, total non-recovering cascade across parallel workers, fresh processes dying at startup — points at **cumulative resource exhaustion on the runner** (handles / named pipes / desktop heap / memory) crossing a threshold, after which no new nvim can start.
>
> Neovim churns pipes and child processes hard on Windows (RPC named pipes, stdio pipes, providers, :make/powershell, server/channel tests), so a per-test leak in the long-lived test host is the most consistent explanation.


## Next steps:

> 1. Log the child exit code on EOF (cheap, cross-platform). On Windows the NTSTATUS immediately classifies it: 0xC0000005 = access violation (real nvim bug), 0xC0000374 = heap corruption, low/clean codes or spawn failure = resource/infra.
> 2. Enable WER LocalDumps for nvim.exe on the Windows runner and upload minidumps as a failure artifact — gives an actual backtrace next occurrence.
> 3. If (1) shows spawn failures/resource errors: add a periodic handle/working-set count to confirm the exhaustion hypothesis and find the leak.

comment_data.body:
After https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/40841 , latest [failure](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/actions/runs/29738289520/job/88338777373) shows: 

```
RUN      T113 python3 provider does not truncate error message <1 MB: 16.42 ms FAIL
D:/a/neovim/neovim/test\functional\testnvim.lua:143: Nvim EOF (crash?) exit code: 3221225794 (0xC0000142)
```


0xC0000142 = `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED`: process failed because a Dynamic Link Library (DLL) could not initialize properly.

Common Causes

- Desktop heap exhaustion, "especially when many processes are repeatedly created" [MSDN](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-erref/596a1078-e883-4972-9bbc-49e60bebca55)
- A dependency (VC++ runtime, etc.) is present but fails to initialize.
- A third-party injected DLL (antivirus, overlay, profiler, shell extension, etc.) failed.

might be caused by test parallelism 😭

Possible root causes specific to Nvim CI:

- the long-lived Lua test runners;
- child processes not fully reaped;
- ConPTY or console-host processes;
- Windows Error Reporting or crash-dialog infrastructure;
- GitHub runner infrastructure;
- some subprocess launched by tests.
